result.summary: The intersection is equipped with high-visibility continental crosswalks and dedicated pedestrian signals, providing a clear path for walkers. However, the presence of large support columns for an elevated structure on the corner creates potential sightline obstructions between motorists and pedestrians. The wide roadway and lack of physical traffic calming measures like curb extensions may also contribute to higher vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Elevated Structure Columns
hazards.description: Large blue metal columns may block the line of sight between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the intersection corner

hazards.name: Wide Turning Radius
hazards.description: The corner geometry allows for relatively high-speed vehicle turns, increasing risk to pedestrians in the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the corners to reduce crossing distance and improve pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval
interventions.description: Program traffic signals to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle traffic gets a green light.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is dominated by a large elevated rail structure that creates significant visual obstructions and deep shadows at a wide intersection. While marked crosswalks are present, the lack of physical refuge and the scale of the roadway prioritize vehicle throughput over pedestrian safety.

hazards.name: Structural Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Large steel support pillars for the elevated rail structure block the view between drivers and pedestrians at the intersection corners.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and center-left, supporting the blue elevated structure

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide multi-lane roadway requires pedestrians to be exposed to traffic for an extended period without a refuge island.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side, marked crosswalk across the main thoroughfare

hazards.name: Deep Shadows
hazards.description: The elevated structure creates high-contrast shadows that can make pedestrians less visible to drivers, especially during transition periods.
hazards.location_in_image: Roadway surface directly beneath the blue structure

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median or refuge island to break up the crossing distance and provide a safe waiting area.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Add bulb-outs at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and move pedestrians into the driver's line of sight beyond the pillars.

interventions.title: Enhanced Under-Structure Lighting
interventions.description: Install high-intensity pedestrian-scale lighting beneath the elevated rail to eliminate dark spots and improve visibility.

result.summary: This wide, multi-lane intersection is dominated by an elevated rail structure that creates significant visual obstructions for both drivers and pedestrians. Although basic infrastructure like sidewalks and crosswalks are present, the long crossing distances and lack of pedestrian protection features make the environment challenging for non-motorized users.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without a refuge island, increasing exposure time to vehicles.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Islands

interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the intersection to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility between users.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Replace standard parallel line markings with continental or ladder style markings for better visibility to approaching drivers.
